questions.prompt: The nearest star to Earth is:
Stars cannot be seen in the day because:
options: they are too dull to be seen against the intense light from the Sun.
they do not exist in that part of the sky seen during the day.
they are blue in colour and so cannot be seen against the blue sky.
questions.explanation: B:the sky is bright from scattered sunlight;most stars are too faint against it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a dwarf planet?
Which of the following has a gravitational force field around it?
options: The person’s soul sitting next to you
Everything with mass has a gravitational force field.
questions.explanation: D:all objects with mass produce gravitational fields.

questions.prompt: As you move away from Earth, its gravitational force field:
questions.explanation: B:gravitational field strength decreases with distance.

questions.prompt: Earth’s axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5°. Imagine it didn’t tilt. Which of the following statements would then be true?
options: Earth would have the same seasons as it does now.
Earth’s seasons would be longer than they are now.
Earth would not have any seasons at all.
The length of the day would change.
questions.explanation: C:no tilt-driven seasons,ignoring the much smaller orbital-eccentricity effect.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about small solar system bodies is true?
options: Most asteroids are located in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Meteors partly burn up as they enter Earth’s atmosphere, the rest striking the surface and leaving craters behind.
Comets are also known as ‘shooting stars’.
Solar winds blow comets towards Earth.
questions.explanation: A:main asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.prompt: Leap years have 1 day added to them. The following key can be used to calculate if any year will or will not be a leap year. Is the year divisible by 400? Yes? The year is a leap year. If not, is the year divisible by 100? Yes? The year is a normal year. If not, is the year divisible by 4? Yes? The year is a leap year. Use this information to calculate which of the following years was a leap year.
questions.explanation: C:1600 is divisible by400;1500,1700,1800are century years not divisible by400.

questions.prompt: The years below were all important years in Australia’s history. Which year was not a leap year?
questions.explanation: B:1901 is not divisible by4. This tests calendar arithmetic;historical event labels are not needed to determine the answer.

questions.prompt: The Moon takes 27.3 days to rotate once on its own axis. It also takes 27.3 days to revolve once around Earth on its orbit. Because of this:
options: on Earth we only ever see one side of the Moon, regardless of where it is in its orbit.
we see a full Moon every 27.3 days.
we only see the Moon once every 27.3 days.
the Moon disappears from view once every 27.3 days.
questions.explanation: A:approximately the same hemisphere faces Earth due to synchronous rotation(small librations allow viewing more than half over time).

questions.prompt: Mnemonics are ways of helping you remember something difficult. They are often used to remember the order of the planets from the Sun. Which of the following mnemonics correctly describes this order?
options: My Vinyl Egg Makes John’s Seem Under Nourished
Nigel’s Under Slime Juice! Michael Existed Very Majestically
Just Sitting Under Neath, Maggie Viewed Every Magpie
Very Many Extra Mice Niggled Some Jelly Up

questions.prompt: The distance from Earth to the Moon is 400 000 km. The distance from Sydney to Cairns is 2000 km. This means that a trip from Earth to the Moon  and back is equivalent to:
options: 200 trips from Sydney to Cairns and back.
400 trips from Sydney to Cairns and back.
100 trips from Sydney to Cairns and back.
2000 trips Sydney to Cairns and back.

questions.prompt: The distance from the Sun to Earth is 150 million kilometres or 150 000 000 km. This distance is also known as the Astronomical Unit (AU). This means that 1 AU = 150 000 000 km. The distance from the Sun to Mars is 230 million kilometres. When Earth and Mars are closest to each other, approximately how far is it between them?
